branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Unilateral Orbital Mass with Skull Base Involvement and Neurological Deficits

state.case_summary:
A 34-year old African American woman with a history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma (treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum) presented with a painless, left upper eyelid mass that had previously been excised on 3 separate occasions outside of our institution. Four months later, the patient presented with painless proptosis. After subsequent treatments, the patient presented with left-sided facial numbness seventeen months later.

Initial presentation showed a left upper eyelid mass. Later examinations revealed proptosis.

- Histopathology: Revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme.- Imaging Studies:  Image Title: MRI of the orbits  Image Description: Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated postgadolinium MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment  Image Title: MRI of the skull base  Image Description: Axial T1-weighted postgadolinium MRI shows tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery with extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus and with mass effect on the left temporal lobe- Genetic Testing: Next-generation sequencing of the tumor demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the partner and localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2)

excluded_candidates: Metastatic disease: less likely due to the patient's history of Hodgkin lymphoma and the distinct histopathological features of the orbital mass
Inflammatory condition: less likely due to the presence of a discrete mass and the lack of inflammatory markers
